shared_elements: carved stone slab/plaque as the support
horizontal band or register running across the upper part of the surface
rectangular framed panel enclosing the central field
justification: Both are stone surfaces organised by a horizontal band across the upper area and by straight framing lines enclosing a central field, and both use very shallow carving with fine linear detail. The decisive difference is content and technique: A is almost entirely abstract, with nested rectangular frames and faint incised marks on a flat plaque, whereas B is a three-dimensional shaped pillar covered with recognisable animal figures in modelled relief arranged in narrative-like registers.
